text: No, the 2025 loss is not yet confirmed as persistent. While Hansen data shows a 13.5 ha tree-cover loss in 2025 (3.9% of the asset), corroboration requires observing the same area in a later year to confirm it hasn’t regrown. The latest available year is 2025, so persistence cannot be established yet. The loss occurred in a native forest context, but its cause (e.g., harvest, fire) and legality remain unknown. The observation is supported by JRC 2020 data showing forest cover in 2020 over the affected area. Further monitoring in 2026+ is needed for confirmation.
